meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me why my son has a zero.
I didn't come in to be thanked. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, with an answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and her questions about who decided it answered.
What moved her: nothing, because no evidence or ownership of the process was offered before the meeting ended.
What cost ground: opening with a thank-you and nothing else, because it gave her no answer and left her in control of the questions.
Try next time: after her first question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put a dated document on the table.
